title.zh: 卷七十 唐書46: 列傳22 元行欽 夏魯奇 姚洪 李嚴 李仁矩 康思立 張敬達
title.en: Volume 70 Book of Later Tang 46: Biographies 22 - Yuan Xingqin, Xia Luqi, Yao Hong, Li Yan, Li Renju, Kang Sili, Zhang Jingda
title.raw: 卷七十 唐書46: 列傳22 元行欽 夏魯奇 姚洪 李嚴 李仁矩 康思立 張敬達 Volume 70 Book of Later Tang 46: Biographies 22 - Yuan Xingqin, Xia Luqi, Yao Hong, Li Yan, Li Renju, Kang Sili, Zhang Jingda

sentences.zh: 元行欽，本幽州劉守光之愛將。

translations.literal: Yuan Xingqin was originally a favored general of Liu Shouguang of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xingqin had originally been a favorite general of Liu Shouguang of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 守光之奪父位也，令行欽攻大恩山，又令殺諸兄弟。

translations.literal: When Shouguang seized his father's position, he ordered Xingqin to attack Mount Da'en and also ordered him to kill his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouguang usurped his father's throne, he sent Xingqin against Mount Da'en and ordered him to kill his brothers as well.

sentences.zh: 天祐九年，周德威攻圍山州，守光困蹙，令行欽於山北募兵，以應契丹。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianyou, Zhou Dewei besieged Shan Prefecture; Shouguang was hard pressed and ordered Xingqin to recruit troops north of the mountains to coordinate with the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou 9, Zhou Dewei besieged Shan Prefecture. With Shouguang cornered, he ordered Xingqin to raise troops north of the mountains to link up with the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 時明宗為將，攻行欽於山北，與之接戰，矢及明宗馬鞍，既而以勢迫來降。

translations.literal: At that time Mingzong was a general; he attacked Xingqin north of the mountains and joined battle with him—an arrow reached Mingzong's saddle, and afterward, pressed by circumstance, Xingqin came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong, then a general, attacked Xingqin in the northern hills. In the fighting an arrow struck Mingzong's saddle; eventually, hard pressed, Xingqin surrendered.

sentences.zh: 明宗憐其有勇，奏隸為假子，後因從征討，恩禮特隆。

translations.literal: Mingzong pitied his courage, memorialized to enroll him as a foster son, and afterward because he followed in campaigns and punishments, favor and ritual were especially lofty.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong admired his bravery, had him enrolled as a foster son, and thereafter treated him with exceptional favor on campaign.

sentences.zh: 常臨敵擒生，必有所獲，名聞軍中。

translations.literal: He often faced the enemy and captured men alive—there was always some gain; his name was heard in the army.
translations.idiomatic: He often took prisoners in battle and always brought back spoils, winning renown throughout the army.

sentences.zh: 莊宗東定趙、魏，選驍健置之麾下，因索行欽，莊宗不得已而遣之。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong in the east pacified Zhao and Wei, selected the fierce and strong and placed them under his banner; because he demanded Xingqin, Zhuangzong had no choice but to send him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong secured Zhao and Wei in the east, he drafted the boldest fighters into his guard. He then demanded Xingqin, and Zhuangzong had no choice but to release him.

sentences.zh: 時有散指揮都頭，名為散員，命行欽為都部署，賜姓，名紹榮。

translations.literal: At that time there was a scattered command commander-in-chief called Scattered Cadre; he appointed Xingqin as overall commander, granted a surname, and named him Shaorong.
translations.idiomatic: There was then a corps of scattered guards called the Scattered Cadre. Zhuangzong made Xingqin their commander, granted him the imperial surname, and gave him the name Shaorong.

sentences.zh: 莊宗好戰，勇於大敵，或臨陣有急兵，行欽必橫身解鬥翼衛之。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong loved battle and was brave before great foes; if in the line of battle there was sudden pressing danger, Xingqin always threw his body across to break the fight and wing-guard him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong loved war and feared no great enemy. Whenever battle turned desperate, Xingqin would throw himself in to break the melee and shield the emperor.

sentences.zh: 莊宗營於德勝也，與汴軍戰於潘張，王師不利，諸軍奔亂。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong encamped at Desheng and battled Bian troops at Panzhang; the royal army was unfavorable and the armies fled in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: At Desheng Zhuangzong fought Bian forces at Panzhang. The royal army faltered and the troops broke in disorder.

sentences.zh: 莊宗得三四騎而旋，中野為汴軍數百騎攢槊攻之，事將不測，行欽識其幟，急馳一騎，奮劍斷二矛，斬一級，汴軍乃解圍，翼莊宗還宮。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong obtained three or four horsemen and turned back; in the open field he was attacked by several hundred Bian horsemen with clustered spears—the affair was about to become unforeseeable; Xingqin recognized their banners, urgently galloped one horse, wielded sword and severed two spears, beheaded one head, and the Bian army then lifted the encirclement and winged Zhuangzong back to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong escaped with only three or four riders. In the open field several hundred Bian horsemen closed in with leveled spears. Xingqin recognized their banners, spurred forward alone, cut down two spears and one enemy, broke the encirclement, and escorted Zhuangzong back to camp.

sentences.zh: 莊宗因流涕言曰：「富貴與卿共之。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong thereupon with flowing tears said: "Wealth and honor I share with you.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong wept and said, "Wealth and honor shall be yours as well as mine.

sentences.zh: 」自是寵冠諸將，官至檢校太傅、忻州刺史。

translations.literal: " From this his favor crowned all generals; his office reached Acting Grand Tutor and Xinzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: " From then on he stood above every general, rising to acting grand tutor and prefect of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗平梁，授武寧軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Liang, he was appointed Wuning Army military governor.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong conquered Liang, he was made military governor of Wuning.

sentences.zh: 嘗因內宴群臣，使相預會，行欽官為保傅，當地褥下坐。

translations.literal: Once because of an inner banquet of the civil and military ministers, he had chancellors join the meeting; Xingqin's office was Guardian and Tutor, and he ought to sit below the floor mat.
translations.idiomatic: At a palace banquet for civil and military officials, Xingqin held the rank of guardian-tutor and was seated below the mat on the floor.

sentences.zh: 酒酣樂作，莊宗敘生平戰陣之事，因左右顧視，曰：「紹榮安在？

translations.literal: Wine deep, music begun, Zhuangzong narrated affairs of battles in his life, and turning to left and right looked and said: "Where is Shaorong?
translations.idiomatic: As the wine flowed and music began, Zhuangzong spoke of his battles and glanced about. "Where is Shaorong?" he asked.

sentences.zh: 」所司奏云：「有敕，使相預會，紹榮散官，殿上無位。

translations.literal: " The responsible office memorialized saying: "There is an edict that chancellors join the meeting; Shaorong is a scattered-rank official—on the hall there is no seat.
translations.idiomatic: " The attendants replied, "By edict only chancellors attend. Shaorong holds scattered rank and has no place in the hall."

sentences.zh: 」莊宗徹會不懌。

translations.literal: " Zhuangzong dispersed the meeting, not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong broke up the banquet in displeasure.

sentences.zh: 翌日，以行欽為同平章事，由是不宴百官於內殿，但宴武臣而已，

translations.literal: The next day he made Xingqin Tongpingzhangshi; from this he no longer banqueted the hundred officials in the inner hall, but banqueted only martial ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he made Xingqin a co-chancellor. After that he ceased entertaining all officials in the inner hall and feasted only his military men.

sentences.zh: 三年，行欽喪婦。

translations.literal: In the third year, Xingqin mourned his wife.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Xingqin's wife died.

sentences.zh: 莊宗有所愛宮人生皇子者，劉皇后心忌之，會行欽入侍，莊宗勞之曰：「紹榮喪婦復娶耶！

translations.literal: Zhuangzong had a beloved palace woman who bore a prince; Empress Liu resented her in heart; when Xingqin entered attendance, Zhuangzong comforted him saying: "Shaorong, your wife died—will you marry again!
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong favored a palace woman who had borne a son, and Empress Liu resented her. When Xingqin came to court, Zhuangzong said, "Shaorong, your wife is dead—will you marry again!

sentences.zh: 吾給爾婚財。

translations.literal: I will supply you marriage wealth.
translations.idiomatic: I will provide your wedding gifts."

sentences.zh: 」皇后指所忌宮人謂莊宗曰：「皇帝憐紹榮，可使為婦。

translations.literal: " The empress pointed at the resented palace woman and told Zhuangzong: "The emperor pities Shaorong—he may be made to take her as wife.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress pointed to the woman and said, "If you pity Shaorong, make her his wife."

sentences.zh: 」莊宗難違所請，微許之。

translations.literal: " Zhuangzong found it hard to refuse what was requested and faintly assented.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong could not easily refuse and gave a reluctant assent.

sentences.zh: 皇后即命紹榮謝之，未退，肩輿已出。

translations.literal: The empress immediately ordered Shaorong to thank her; he had not yet withdrawn when the sedan chair had already gone out.
translations.idiomatic: The empress had Shaorong thank her at once. Before he could withdraw, the woman was sent out in a sedan chair.

sentences.zh: 莊宗心不懌，佯不豫者累日，業已遣去，無如之何。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong's heart was not pleased; he feigned displeasure for many days—already sent away, nothing to be done about it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was displeased and for days pretended illness, but the marriage was already done and could not be undone.

sentences.zh: 及貝州軍亂，趙在禮入魏州，莊宗方擇將，皇后曰：「小事不勞大將，促紹榮指揮可也。

translations.literal: When the Bei Prefecture army rebelled and Zhao Zaili entered Wei Prefecture, Zhuangzong was just selecting a general; the empress said: "Small affairs need not trouble great generals—urge Shaorong to command and it will do.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion broke out at Bei Prefecture and Zhao Zaili seized Wei, Zhuangzong was choosing a commander. The empress said, "This is a small matter—send Shaorong and it will suffice."

sentences.zh: 」乃以行欽為鄴都行營招撫使，領騎二千進討。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Xingqin was made Ye Capital Campaign Recruit-and-Pacify Commissioner, leading two thousand cavalry to advance and punish.
translations.idiomatic: Xingqin was made commissioner to pacify the Ye capital region and led two thousand horsemen against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 洎至鄴城，攻之不能下，退保於澶州。

translations.literal: When he reached Ye city he could not take it by attack and withdrew to guard at Dan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He failed to take Ye and withdrew to Danzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，諸道之師稍集，復進軍於鄴城之南。

translations.literal: Before long the armies of the various circuits gradually gathered, and again advanced the army south of Ye city.
translations.idiomatic: Soon troops from the provinces assembled, and he advanced again south of Ye.

sentences.zh: 及明宗為帥，領軍至鄴，行欽來謁於軍中，拜起之際，誤呼萬歲者再，明宗驚駭，遏之方止。

translations.literal: When Mingzong was commander and led the army to Ye, Xingqin came to call on him in the army; as he bowed and rose, he mistakenly shouted "Long live!" twice; Mingzong was startled and alarmed, and only after restraining him did it stop.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong arrived at Ye as commander, Xingqin came to his camp. Rising from a bow, he twice cried "Long live the emperor!" Mingzong was shocked and had to silence him.

sentences.zh: 既而明宗營於城西，行欽營於城南。

translations.literal: Afterward Mingzong encamped west of the city and Xingqin encamped south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong then encamped west of the city and Xingqin south of it.

sentences.zh: 三月八日夜，明宗為亂軍所迫，惟行欽之軍不動，按甲以自固。

translations.literal: On the night of the eighth day of the third month, Mingzong was pressed by the mutinous army; only Xingqin's army did not move, holding armor to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the eighth of the third month the mutineers pressed Mingzong. Only Xingqin's troops held firm under arms.

sentences.zh: 明宗密令張虔釗至行欽營，戒之曰：「且堅壁勿動，計會同殺亂軍，莫錯疑誤。

translations.literal: Mingzong secretly ordered Zhang Qianzhao to Xingqin's camp and warned him: "For now hold the walls and do not move; plan together to kill the mutinous army—do not wrongly suspect in error.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong secretly sent Zhang Qianzhao to warn him, "Hold your position and do not stir. We shall join to destroy the mutineers—do not mistake friend for foe."

sentences.zh: 」行欽不聽，將步騎萬人棄甲而退。

translations.literal: " Xingqin would not listen and led ten thousand foot and horse, casting off armor and withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: Xingqin would not listen. He led ten thousand men, cast off their armor, and retreated.

sentences.zh: 自知失策，且保衛州，因誣奏明宗曰：「鎮師已入賊軍，終不為國使。

translations.literal: Knowing he had lost his plan, he moreover guarded Weizhou and thereupon falsely memorialized Mingzong saying: "The campaign army has already entered the rebel army and in the end will not act for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his error, he withdrew to Weizhou and falsely reported that Mingzong had gone over to the rebels and would never serve the throne.

sentences.zh: 」明宗既劫出鄴城，令人走馬上章，申理其事，言：「臣且於近郡聽進止。

translations.literal: " Mingzong, already seized out of Ye city, had a man gallop up and memorialize, explaining the affair, saying: "Your subject will for the moment in nearby commanderies listen for advance or halt.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong, already forced from Ye, sent a rider with a memorial explaining himself: "I shall await orders in the nearest prefecture."

sentences.zh: 」莊宗覽奏釋然曰：「吾知紹榮妄矣。

translations.literal: " Zhuangzong reading the memorial was relieved and said: "I know Shaorong is reckless.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong read it and said with relief, "I knew Shaorong was lying."

sentences.zh: 」因令白從訓與明宗子繼璟至軍前，欲令見明宗，行欽縶繼璟於路。

translations.literal: " He thereupon ordered Bai Congxun and Mingzong's son Jijian to the army front, wishing to have them see Mingzong; Xingqin bound Jijian on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Bai Congxun and Mingzong's son Jijian to the front to summon Mingzong, but Xingqin seized Jijian on the road.

sentences.zh: 明宗凡奏軍機，拘留不達，故旬日之間，音驛斷絕。

translations.literal: Whatever military reports Mingzong memorialized, Xingqin detained and did not deliver; thus within ten days or so, sound and post were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: He detained Mingzong's military reports, and for ten days no word reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗出成皋，知明宗在黎陽，復令繼璟渡河召明宗，行欽即殺之，仍勸班師。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong went out to Chenggao and knew Mingzong was at Liyang, he again ordered Jijian to cross the river and summon Mingzong; Xingqin then killed him and still urged withdrawal of the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong moved to Chenggao and learned Mingzong was at Liyang, he again sent Jijian across the river. Xingqin killed him and urged retreat.

sentences.zh: 四月一日，莊宗既崩，行欽引皇后、存渥，得七百騎出師子門，將之河中就存霸，沿路部下解散，從者數騎而已。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fourth month Zhuangzong had already died; Xingqin led the empress and Cunwo, obtaining seven hundred horsemen, went out Shizi Gate, intending to go to Hedong to join Cunba; along the road subordinates dispersed—only several horsemen followed.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of the fourth month Zhuangzong was dead. Xingqin led the empress and Cunwo with seven hundred horsemen out Shizi Gate toward Hedong to Cunba. Along the way his followers scattered until only a few riders remained.

sentences.zh: 四日，至平陸縣界，為百姓所擒，縣令裴進折其足，檻車以獻。

translations.literal: On the fourth day, reaching the border of Pinglu County, he was seized by the common people; Magistrate Pei Jin broke his feet and sent him in a caged cart as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth, at Pinglu County, commoners seized him. Magistrate Pei Jin broke his feet and sent him in a cage-cart as a captive.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，詔削奪行欽在位官爵，斬於洛陽。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, an edict stripped Xingqin of his offices and titles in position, and he was beheaded at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong came to the throne, he stripped Xingqin of rank and beheaded him at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 夏魯奇，字邦傑，青州人也。

translations.literal: Xia Luqi, style Bangjie, was a man of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Luqi, courtesy name Bangjie, was a native of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 初事宣武軍為軍校，與主將不協，遂歸於莊宗，以為護衛指揮使。

translations.literal: At first he served the Xuanwu Army as a military school officer; he did not harmonize with the chief general and thereupon returned to Zhuangzong, who made him a guard commander.
translations.idiomatic: He first served the Xuanwu army as an officer. Falling out with his commander, he went over to Zhuangzong and became a guard commander.

sentences.zh: 從周德威攻幽州，燕將有單廷珪、元行欽，時稱驍勇，魯奇與之鬥，兩不能解，將士皆釋兵縱觀。

translations.literal: Following Zhou Dewei in attacking Youzhou, among Yan generals were Shan Tinggui and Yuan Xingqin, then called fierce and brave; Luqi battled with them—neither could resolve it, and officers and soldiers all laid down weapons and watched freely.
translations.idiomatic: In the attack on Youzhou with Zhou Dewei, the Yan generals Shan Tinggui and Yuan Xingqin were famed for valor. Luqi fought them to a standstill while the troops laid down their arms and watched.

sentences.zh: 幽州平，魯奇功居多。

translations.literal: When Youzhou was pacified, Luqi's merit was comparatively the greater.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhou fell, Luqi's merit ranked among the highest.

sentences.zh: 梁將劉鄩在洹水，莊宗深入致師，鄩設伏於魏縣西南葭蘆中。

translations.literal: Liang General Liu Yan was at Huanshui; Zhuangzong went deep to bring troops to battle, and Yan set an ambush in the reed-rushes southwest of Wei County.
translations.idiomatic: Liang general Liu Yan held Huanshui. Zhuangzong advanced deep into enemy country, and Yan ambushed him in the reed marshes southwest of Wei County.

sentences.zh: 莊宗不滿千騎，汴人伏兵萬餘，大噪而起，圍莊宗數重。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong had not full thousand horsemen; Bian men's ambush troops were more than ten thousand; with great clamor they rose and encircled Zhuangzong in many layers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong had fewer than a thousand horsemen. More than ten thousand Bian ambushers sprang up with a roar and surrounded him many ranks deep.

sentences.zh: 魯奇與王門關、烏德兒等奮命決戰，自午至申，俄而李存審兵至方解。

translations.literal: Luqi with Wang Menguan, Wu De'er, and others fought desperately from noon to the shen hour; presently Li Cunjian's troops arrived and only then was it resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Luqi, Wang Menguan, Wu De'er, and others fought desperately from noon until mid-afternoon before Li Cunjian's relief arrived.

sentences.zh: 魯奇持槍攜劍，獨衛莊宗，手殺百餘人。

translations.literal: Luqi held spear and carried sword, alone guarding Zhuangzong, with his hand killing more than a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Luqi, spear in hand and sword at his side, alone shielded Zhuangzong and killed more than a hundred men himself.

sentences.zh: 烏德兒等被擒，魯奇傷痍遍體，自是莊宗尤憐之，曆磁州刺史。

translations.literal: Wu De'er and others were captured; Luqi's wounds covered his body; from this Zhuangzong especially pitied him and passed through Cizhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Wu De'er was captured. Luqi was covered with wounds, and Zhuangzong thereafter favored him greatly, later making him prefect of Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 中都之戰，汴人大敗，魯奇見王彥章，識之，單馬追及，槍擬其頸；

translations.literal: In the battle of Zhongdu, Bian men were greatly defeated; Luqi saw Wang Yanzhang, recognized him, and alone on horse pursued and caught up, spear set to his neck;
translations.idiomatic: At Zhongdu the Bian army was routed. Luqi recognized Wang Yanzhang, chased him down alone, and set his spear to Yanzhang's neck.

sentences.zh: 彥章顧曰：「爾非餘故人乎？

translations.literal: Yanzhang turned his head and said: "Are you not my old acquaintance?
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang looked back and said, "Are you not an old friend of mine?"

sentences.zh: 」即擒之以獻。

translations.literal: " He thereupon seized him and presented him.
translations.idiomatic: " Luqi seized him and brought him in.

sentences.zh: 莊宗壯之，賞絹千匹。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong deemed it strong and rewarded a thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was impressed and rewarded him with a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·趙庭隱傳》：王彥章守中都，庭隱在其軍中。

translations.literal: (From the "Biography of Zhao Tingyin" in the Records of the Nine States: Wang Yanzhang defended Zhongdu, and Tingyin was in his army.
translations.idiomatic: (From the "Biography of Zhao Tingyin" in the Records of the Nine States: Wang Yanzhang held Zhongdu, and Tingyin served in his army.

sentences.zh: 及彥章敗，庭隱為莊宗所獲，將以就戮，大將夏魯奇奏曰：「此矬也，其材可用。

translations.literal: When Yanzhang was defeated, Tingyin was taken by Zhuangzong and was about to be put to death; great general Xia Luqi memorialized saying: "This is a dwarf—his talent can be used.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanzhang fell, Zhuangzong captured Tingyin and was about to execute him. Grand general Xia Luqi said, "This short fellow still has his uses."

sentences.zh: 」遂釋之。）〉

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was released.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " He was spared.)〉

sentences.zh: 梁平，授鄭州防禦使。

translations.literal: Liang pacified, he was appointed Zhengzhou Defense Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang was pacified, he was made defense commissioner of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，授河陽節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Heyang military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became military governor of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 天成初，移鎮許州，加同平章事。

translations.literal: Early in Tiancheng he was moved to command Xuzhou and added Tongpingzhangshi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiancheng he was transferred to Xuzhou and made co-chancellor.

sentences.zh: 魯奇性忠義，尤通吏道，撫民有術。

translations.literal: Luqi's nature was loyal and righteous, especially penetrating in officials' ways, and in soothing the people he had method.
translations.idiomatic: Luqi was loyal and upright, skilled in administration, and knew how to govern the people.

sentences.zh: 及移鎮許田，孟州之民，萬眾遮道，斷鐙臥轍，五日不發。

translations.literal: When he moved to command Xutian, the people of Meng Prefecture, tens of thousands, blocked the road, broke stirrups and lay across wheels—five days they did not depart.
translations.idiomatic: When he was transferred to Xutian, tens of thousands of people from Mengzhou blocked the road, pulling stirrups and lying across wheels, and for five days he could not leave.

sentences.zh: 父老詣闕請留，明宗令中使諭之，方得離州。

translations.literal: Elders went to the gate to request he remain; Mingzong ordered a palace envoy to instruct them, and only then could he leave the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The elders petitioned the throne to keep him. Mingzong sent an envoy to persuade them, and only then did he leave.

sentences.zh: 明宗討荊南，魯奇為副招討使，頃之，移鎮遂州。

translations.literal: Mingzong punished Jingnan; Luqi was deputy recruit-and-pacify commissioner; soon he was moved to command Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong campaigned against Jingnan, Luqi served as deputy pacification commissioner, then was transferred to Suizhou.

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·李仁罕傳》：夏魯奇稟朝廷之命，繕治甲兵，將圖蜀，孟知祥與董璋謀先取魯奇，令仁罕攻遂州。）〉

translations.literal: (From the "Biography of Li Renhan" in the Records of the Nine States: Xia Luqi received the court's orders, repaired armor and weapons, and was about to scheme against Shu; Meng Zhixiang and Dong Zhang plotted to take Luqi first and ordered Renhan to attack Suizhou.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (From the "Biography of Li Renhan" in the Records of the Nine States: Xia Luqi, acting on court orders, repaired armor and weapons and prepared to move against Shu. Meng Zhixiang and Dong Zhang plotted to strike him first and ordered Renhan to attack Suizhou.)〉

sentences.zh: 董璋之叛，與孟知祥攻遂州，援路斷絕，兵盡食窮，

translations.literal: Dong Zhang's rebellion joined with Meng Zhixiang in attacking Suizhou; the relief road was cut off, troops exhausted and food exhausted,
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhang rebelled, he and Meng Zhixiang attacked Suizhou together. Relief was cut off, and the garrison ran out of food,

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·李肇傳》：蜀師圍夏魯奇於遂州，唐師來援，劍門不守，肇領兵赴普安以拒之，唐師不得進。）〉

translations.literal: (From the "Biography of Li Zhao" in the Records of the Nine States: Shu troops besieged Xia Luqi at Suizhou; Tang troops came to relieve; Jianmen was not held; Zhao led troops to Pu'an to resist them, and the Tang troops could not advance.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (From the "Biography of Li Zhao" in the Records of the Nine States: Shu forces besieged Xia Luqi at Suizhou. Tang relief troops came up, but Jianmen was lost. Zhao led troops to Pu'an to block them, and the Tang army could not advance.)〉

sentences.zh: 魯奇自刎而卒，時年四十九。

translations.literal: Luqi killed himself with a sword and died, at that time age forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Luqi killed himself with his sword. He was forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 帝聞其死也，慟哭之，厚給其家，贈太師、齊國公。

translations.literal: The emperor hearing of his death mourned with weeping, richly supplied his family, and posthumously awarded Grand Preceptor and Duke of Qi State.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of his death he wept, richly rewarded his family, and posthumously made him Grand Preceptor and Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 姚洪，本梁之小校也。

translations.literal: Yao Hong was originally a petty officer of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong had originally been a junior officer of Liang.

sentences.zh: 在梁時，經事董璋，長興初，率兵千人戍閬州。

translations.literal: In Liang times he had served Dong Zhang; early in Changxing he led a thousand troops to garrison Lang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he had served Dong Zhang. Early in Changxing he led a thousand men to garrison Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 璋叛，領眾攻閬州，璋密令人誘洪，洪以大義拒之。

translations.literal: Zhang rebelled and led masses to attack Lang Prefecture; Zhang secretly sent a man to entice Hong, and Hong with great righteousness refused him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang rebelled and attacked Langzhou, he secretly tried to win Hong over, but Hong refused on grounds of loyalty.

sentences.zh: 及璋攻城，洪悉力拒守者三日，禦備既竭，城陷被擒。

translations.literal: When Zhang attacked the city, Hong exhausted his strength resisting for three days; defenses already spent, the city fell and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Hong defended with all his strength for three days. When supplies were spent the city fell and he was taken.

sentences.zh: 璋謂洪曰：「爾頃為健兒，由吾獎拔至此；

translations.literal: Zhang said to Hong: "You in the past were a strong soldier—through my praise and promotion you reached here;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang said to him, "You were once a brave soldier whom I raised to your post.

sentences.zh: 吾書誘諭，投之於側，何相負耶？

translations.literal: I wrote letters enticing and instructing and cast them aside—how do you betray me?
translations.idiomatic: I sent you letters of persuasion, and you cast them aside. How can you say I betrayed you?"

sentences.zh: 」洪大罵曰：「老賊，爾為天子鎮帥，何苦反耶！

translations.literal: " Hong greatly cursed saying: "Old bandit, you were the Son of Heaven's frontier commander—why painfully rebel?
translations.idiomatic: " Hong cursed him loudly: "Old bandit! You were the Son of Heaven's frontier commander—why turn rebel?"

sentences.zh: 爾既辜恩背主，吾與爾何恩，而雲相負！

translations.literal: You have already betrayed grace and turned your back on your lord—what grace do I have with you, that you speak of mutual betrayal!
translations.idiomatic: You have betrayed your sovereign—what debt do I owe you that you speak of betrayal?"

sentences.zh: 爾為李七郎奴，掃馬糞，得一臠殘炙，感恩無盡。

translations.literal: You were Li the Seventh's slave, sweeping horse dung, and got one scrap of leftover meat—gratitude without end.
translations.idiomatic: You were slave to Li the Seventh, sweeping horse dung, and were grateful for a scrap of meat.

sentences.zh: 今明天子付與茅土，貴為諸侯，而驅徒結黨，圖為反噬。

translations.literal: Now the bright Son of Heaven has entrusted you with feudal soil, noble as the feudal lords, yet you drive followers and knot factions, scheming to turn and bite.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Son of Heaven has made you a feudal lord, yet you gather ruffians and plot treason."

sentences.zh: 爾本奴才，則無恥；

translations.literal: You are originally a slave fellow—then without shame;
translations.idiomatic: You were born a slave and know no shame.

sentences.zh: 吾忠義之士，不忍為也。

translations.literal: I am a loyal and righteous man and cannot bear to do it.
translations.idiomatic: I am a man of loyalty and will not live as another's slave."

sentences.zh: 吾可為天子死，不能與人奴苟生！

translations.literal: I can die for the Son of Heaven and cannot with another's slave live in compromise!
translations.idiomatic: I would die for the Son of Heaven rather than live cringing to a rebel's slave!"

sentences.zh: 」璋怒，令軍士十人，持刀刲割其膚，燃鑊於前，自取啖食，洪至死大罵不已。

translations.literal: " Zhang in anger ordered ten soldiers with knives to slice and cut his flesh, a cauldron burning before him; Hong himself took and ate it, and Hong to death greatly cursed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang in rage had ten soldiers slice his flesh while a cauldron boiled before him. Hong ate the pieces himself and cursed without cease until he died.

sentences.zh: 明宗聞之泣下，置洪二子於近衛，給賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Mingzong hearing it wept; he placed Hong's two sons in the close guard and gave rewards very thick.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong wept when he heard it, enrolled Hong's two sons in the close guard, and gave them rich rewards.

sentences.zh: 李嚴，幽州人，本名讓坤。

translations.literal: Li Yan, a man of Youzhou, original name Rangkun.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan, a native of Youzhou, was originally named Rangkun.

sentences.zh: 初仕燕，為刺史，涉獵書傳，便弓馬，有口辯，多遊藝，以功名自許。

translations.literal: At first he served Yan as prefect, ranged through books and transmissions, was skilled at bow and horse, had eloquence of mouth, much wandered in arts, and with merit and fame made himself his pledge.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Yan as prefect, studied the classics, excelled at archery and horsemanship, was eloquent and accomplished in many arts, and aimed at achievement and fame.

sentences.zh: 同光中，為客省使。

translations.literal: In Tongguang he was Guest Repository Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tongguang era he became guest repository commissioner.

sentences.zh: 奉使於蜀，及與王衍相見，陳使者之禮，因於笏記中具述莊宗興復之功，其警句云：「才過汶水，縛王彥章於馬前；

translations.literal: Sent on mission to Shu, when he met Wang Yan he set forth the envoy's ritual; thereupon in his tablet memorandum he fully narrated Zhuangzong's restoration merit; its alert lines said: "Talent just passed Wenshui, bound Wang Yanzhang before the horse;
translations.idiomatic: On embassy to Shu he met Wang Yan and observed diplomatic ritual. In his memorandum on the tablet he recounted Zhuangzong's restoration: "Just past Wenshui, Wang Yanzhang was bound before the horse;

sentences.zh: 旋及夷門，斬朱友貞於樓上。

translations.literal: turning to Yimen, Zhu Youzhen was beheaded atop the tower.
translations.idiomatic: soon at Yimen, Zhu Youzhen was beheaded on the tower."

sentences.zh: 」嚴復聲韻清亮，蜀人聽之愕然。

translations.literal: " Yan again spoke with clear, bright tone and rhythm; the people of Shu heard it and were startled.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan recited it again in a clear, resonant voice. The Shu listeners were stunned.

sentences.zh: 時蜀偽樞密使宋光嗣召嚴曲宴，因以近事訊於嚴。

translations.literal: At that time the Shu false privy councilor Song Guangsi summoned Yan to a private banquet and thereupon inquired of recent affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu privy councilor Song Guangsi then invited Yan to a private banquet and questioned him about recent events.

sentences.zh: 嚴對曰：「吾皇前年四月即位於鄴宮，當月下鄆州。

translations.literal: Yan replied: "Our emperor in the fourth month two years ago took the throne at the Ye palace; that same month he descended on Yun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied, "Our emperor took the throne at Ye in the fourth month two years ago and that same month marched on Yun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十月四日，親統萬騎破賊中都，乘勝鼓行，遂誅汴孽，偽梁尚有兵三十萬，謀臣猛將，解甲倒戈。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the tenth month he personally commanded ten thousand horsemen and broke the rebels at Zhongdu; riding victory he beat the drums and advanced, and thereupon executed the Bian remnant; false Liang still had three hundred thousand troops, but strategists and fierce generals doffed armor and turned their blades.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the tenth month he personally led ten thousand horsemen and smashed the enemy at Zhongdu. Pressing the victory, he marched on and destroyed the Bian remnant. Though false Liang still had three hundred thousand troops, its strategists and fierce generals laid down their arms and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 西盡甘、涼，東漸海外，南逾閩、浙，北極幽陵。

translations.literal: West to the limit of Gan and Liang, east gradually to beyond the seas, south crossing Min and Zhe, north to the utmost of Youling.
translations.idiomatic: His realm reached west to Gan and Liang, east to the sea, south beyond Min and Zhe, and north to Youling.

sentences.zh: 牧伯侯王，稱藩不暇，家財入貢，府實上供。

translations.literal: Pastoral lords, marquises, and kings declare vassalage without respite; household wealth enters as tribute and storehouse goods are sent up in supply.
translations.idiomatic: Regional lords and petty kings line up to swear fealty, pouring private fortunes and provincial treasuries into tribute.

sentences.zh: 吳國本朝舊臣，岐下先皇元老，遣子入侍，述職稱藩。

translations.literal: Wu is an old minister of this dynasty; the senior elders at Qi send their sons to attend court, report duty, and declare vassalage.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, once a loyal subject of our house, and the veteran statesmen at Qi send their sons to court to renew their vows of vassalage.

sentences.zh: 淮、海之君，卑辭厚貢，湖湘、荊楚，杭越、甌閩，異貨奇珍，府無虛月。

translations.literal: The lords of Huai and the sea use humble words and thick tribute; Huguang, Jing-Chu, Hang-Yue, Ou-Min—exotic goods and rare treasures—the treasury has no empty month.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers along the Huai and the coast come with humble words and lavish gifts. From Hunan, Hubei, the lower Yangtze, Hangzhou, Yue, Wenzhou, and Fujian flow exotic goods and rarities, so the imperial stores never stand idle a single month.

sentences.zh: 吾皇以德懷來，以威款附。

translations.literal: Our emperor by virtue cherishes and draws them in; by majesty he wins their heartfelt attachment.
translations.idiomatic: Our emperor draws men in through virtue and binds them through power.

sentences.zh: 順則涵之以恩澤，逆則問之以干戈，四海車書，大同非晚。

translations.literal: If compliant, he envelops them with grace and favor; if rebellious, he inquires of them with weapons and armor; within the four seas, chariots and writing—Great Unity is not far off.
translations.idiomatic: The obedient he rewards with grace; the defiant he answers with arms. When chariots and written law span the four seas, universal empire will come soon.

sentences.zh: 」光嗣曰：「餘所未知，惟岐下宋公，我之姻好，洞見其心，反覆多端，專謀跋扈，大不足信也。

translations.literal: " Guangsi said: "Of the rest I do not know; only Duke Song of Qi, my marriage kin—I see through his heart—turning and turning many ways, devoted to plotting overbearing sway, greatly not to be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: " Guangsi said, "Of the rest I cannot say. Only Duke Song of Qi, bound to me by marriage—I know his heart well. He is fickle and scheming, bent on arrogance and power, and utterly untrustworthy.

sentences.zh: 似聞契丹部族，近日稍強，大國可無慮乎？

translations.literal: It seems I hear the Khitan tribal groups have lately grown somewhat strong—can the great state be without concern?
translations.idiomatic: I hear the Khitan tribes have grown stronger lately. Surely the great power has nothing to fear?

sentences.zh: 」嚴曰：「子言契丹之強盛，孰若偽梁？

translations.literal: " Yan said: "You speak of Khitan strength and prosperity—which is it like, the pseudo-Liang?
translations.idiomatic: " Yan said, "You ask about Khitan might—which do you mean, the pseudo-Liang?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「比梁差劣也。

translations.literal: " He said: "Compared with Liang they are somewhat inferior.
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "They fall short of Liang."

sentences.zh: 」嚴曰：「吾國視契丹如蚤虱耳，以其無害，不足爬搔。

translations.literal: " Yan said: "Our state regards the Khitan like fleas and lice—for they are harmless, not worth scratching and picking.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan said, "We regard the Khitan as fleas and lice—harmless vermin not worth troubling ourselves over.

sentences.zh: 吾良將勁兵布天下，彼不勞一郡之兵，一校之眾，則懸首槀街，盡為奴擄。

translations.literal: Our good generals and strong troops are spread over all under Heaven; they need not trouble one commandery's troops or one commandant's multitude—then heads hung on the public street, all made slaves and captives.
translations.idiomatic: Our finest generals and toughest troops are posted across the realm. Without mustering so much as a single prefecture or one company, we could hang their heads in the marketplace and make them all slaves.

sentences.zh: 但以天生四夷，當置度外，不在九州之本，未欲窮兵黷武也。

translations.literal: Only because the Heaven-born Four Yi ought be set beyond measure, not within the Nine Regions' root—we do not yet wish to exhaust troops and abuse warfare.
translations.idiomatic: But the barbarians of the four directions are born beyond our core lands, and we do not wish to waste strength in endless war.

sentences.zh: 」光嗣聞辯對，畏而奇之。

translations.literal: " Guangsi heard the eloquent reply, feared it, and marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: " Guangsi, hearing this sharp reply, was both afraid and astonished.

sentences.zh: 時王衍失政，嚴知其可取，使還具奏，故平蜀之謀，始於嚴。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Yan's governance was lost; Yan knew he could be taken, sent back to submit a full report—thus the scheme to pacify Shu began with Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan was misruling Shu, and Yan saw he could be conquered. He returned and filed a full report, and the plan to conquer Shu began with Yan.

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜起軍之日，以嚴為三川招撫使，嚴與先鋒使康延孝將兵五千，先驅閣道，或馳以詞說，或威以兵鋒，大軍未及，所在降下。

translations.literal: On the day Guo Chongyao raised troops, Yan was made Commissioner to Recruit and Pacify the Three Rivers; Yan with vanguard commissioner Kang Yanxiao led five thousand troops, advancing first on the plank roads—sometimes galloping with rhetoric to persuade, sometimes aweing with military edge; the great army had not yet arrived, and wherever they went submissions descended.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Chongyao took the field, Yan was made commissioner to win over the Three Circuits. He and the vanguard commander Kang Yanxiao led five thousand men ahead along the mountain roads, sometimes galloping ahead to persuade by word, sometimes brandishing arms. Before the main army arrived, posts along the way surrendered.

sentences.zh: 延孝在漢州，王衍與書曰：「 可請李司空先來，餘即舉城納款。

translations.literal: Yanxiao was at Han Prefecture; Wang Yan sent him a letter saying: "You may request Vice Minister Li to come first; I will then raise the city and offer submission.
translations.idiomatic: At Hanzhou, Wang Yan wrote Yanxiao: "Ask Vice Minister Li to come first, and I will surrender the city.

sentences.zh: 」眾咸以討蜀之謀始於嚴，衍以甘言，將誘而殺之，欲不令往。

translations.literal: " The crowd all held that the scheme to attack Shu began with Yan; Yan intended with sweet words to lure and kill him—they wished not to let him go.
translations.idiomatic: " Everyone said the Shu campaign had begun with Yan, and that Wang Yan's flattery was a trap to lure and kill him; they urged Yan not to go.

sentences.zh: 嚴聞之喜，即馳騎入益州，衍見嚴於母前，以母、妻為托。

translations.literal: Yan heard it and rejoiced, immediately galloping on horseback into Yi Prefecture; Yan met Yan before his mother, entrusting mother and wife to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was delighted and rode at once into Yizhou. Wang Yan received him before his mother and entrusted his mother and wife to Yan's care.

sentences.zh: 即日，引蜀使歐陽彬迎謁魏王繼岌。

translations.literal: That same day he led the Shu envoy Ouyang Bin to meet and pay respects to Prince of Wei Jiji.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he presented the Shu envoy Ouyang Bin to Prince of Wei Jiji.

sentences.zh: 蜀平班師，會明宗即位，遷泗州防禦使兼客省使。

translations.literal: Shu pacified, the army withdrew; coinciding with Mingzong's accession, he was moved to Sizhou Defense Commissioner and concurrently Guest Repository Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu was pacified and the troops withdrew, Mingzong came to the throne and Yan was made defense commissioner of Sizhou and concurrently commissioner of the guest repository.

sentences.zh: 長興初，安重誨謀欲控製兩川，嚴乃求為西川兵馬都監，庶效方略。

translations.literal: Early in Changxing, An Chonghui schemed wishing to control the Two Rivers; Yan then requested to be Western Rivers military superintendent, hoping to offer strategems.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Changxing era An Chonghui sought to tighten control over the Two Shu circuits, and Yan asked to be made military superintendent of Western Shu so he could put his plans to use.

sentences.zh: 孟知祥覺之，既至，執而害之。

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang perceived it; once he arrived, he seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang saw through the move, and when Yan arrived he seized and killed him.

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·王彥銖傳》：李嚴之為監軍也，密懷異謀，知祥數其過，命彥銖擒斬之，嚴之左右無敢動者。）〉

translations.literal: (From the "Biography of Wang Yanzhu" in the Records of the Nine States: When Li Yan served as military superintendent, he secretly harbored a divergent scheme; Zhixiang counted his offenses and ordered Yanzhu to seize and behead him—none of Yan's attendants dared move.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (From the "Biography of Wang Yanzhu" in the Records of the Nine States: While serving as superintendent, Li Yan plotted treason in secret. Meng Zhixiang listed his crimes and ordered Wang Yanzhu to seize and execute him; none of Yan's attendants dared stir.)〉

sentences.zh: 贈太保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 嚴之母，賢明婦人。

translations.literal: Yan's mother was a worthy and enlightened woman.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's mother was a wise and virtuous woman.

sentences.zh: 初，嚴將赴蜀，母曰：「汝前啟破蜀之謀，今又入蜀，將死報蜀人矣！

translations.literal: At first, when Yan was about to go to Shu, his mother said: "You once opened the scheme to break Shu; now you enter Shu again—you will die repaying the people of Shu!
translations.idiomatic: Before Yan set out for Shu, his mother said: "You first devised the plan to conquer Shu, and now you go back—you will die at the hands of the Shu people!

sentences.zh: 與汝永訣。

translations.literal: I take everlasting leave of you.
translations.idiomatic: This is our final parting."

sentences.zh: 」既而果如其言。

translations.literal: " Afterward it indeed came about as she had said.
translations.idiomatic: " Events unfolded exactly as she had foretold.

sentences.zh: 李仁矩，本明宗在藩鎮時客將也。

translations.literal: Li Renju had originally been a guest officer when Mingzong was at his fief.
translations.idiomatic: Li Renju had been a client officer in Mingzong's service when he still held a fief.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，錄其趨走之勞，擢居內職，復為安重誨所庇，故數年之間，遷為客省使、左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, he recorded Renju's running-about labors, promoted him to inner-office posts, and again he was sheltered by An Chonghui—thus within several years he was moved to Guest Repository Commissioner and Left Guard Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: After Mingzong came to the throne he rewarded Renju's years of service and raised him to inner-court posts. Protected by An Chonghui, within a few years he became guest repository commissioner and left guard grand general.

sentences.zh: 天成中，因奉使東川，董璋張筵以召之，仁矩貪於館舍，與倡妓酣飲，日既中而不至，大為璋所詬辱，自是深銜之。

translations.literal: In the Tiancheng era, because he went on mission to Eastern Rivers, Dong Zhang spread a banquet to summon him; Renju, greedy for the lodge quarters, drank deeply with singing girls and prostitutes—the sun already at midday and he did not arrive—greatly was he reviled and shamed by Zhang; from this he deeply bore resentment.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiancheng he went on mission to Eastern Shu. Dong Zhang invited him to a feast, but Renju lingered in his quarters drinking with entertainers until midday and never appeared. Zhang publicly humiliated him, and from that day Renju hated him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 長興初，璋既跋扈於東川，重誨奏以仁矩為閬州節度使，俾伺璋之反狀，時物議以為不可。

translations.literal: Early in Changxing, Zhang had already been overbearing in Eastern Rivers; Chonghui memorialized making Renju Langzhou military governor, to spy on Zhang's rebellious signs—at the time public opinion held it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Changxing, with Dong Zhang already defiant in Eastern Shu, An Chonghui had Renju appointed military governor of Langzhou to watch for rebellion. Public opinion at the time held the move unwise.

sentences.zh: 及仁矩至鎮，偵璋所為，曲形奏報，地裏遐僻，朝廷莫知事實，激成璋之逆節，由仁矩也。

translations.literal: When Renju reached his command, he spied on Zhang's actions and twistedly shaped memorial reports; the locality was remote and secluded—the court did not know the facts—stirring Zhang's rebellious conduct; it was because of Renju.
translations.idiomatic: Once Renju took up his post he spied on Zhang and sent distorted reports. The region was remote, and the court knew nothing of the truth. Renju thus provoked Zhang into open rebellion.

sentences.zh: 長興元年冬十月，璋自率凶黨，以攻其城。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the first year of Changxing, Zhang himself led fierce partisans to attack his city.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Changxing 1, Zhang personally led his ruffians to assault the city.

sentences.zh: 仁矩召軍校謀守戰利害，皆曰：「璋久圖反計，以賂誘士心，凶氣方盛，未可與戰，宜堅壁以守之。

translations.literal: Renju summoned military officers to discuss the gains and losses of defense and battle; all said: "Zhang long plotted rebellion, using bribes to entice soldiers' hearts—the fierce spirit just then flourishing—not yet possible to battle; it is fitting to strengthen walls and defend.
translations.idiomatic: Renju called his officers to weigh defense against attack. They all said: "Zhang has long plotted rebellion and bought the troops' loyalty. His momentum is too strong to meet in the field. Hold the walls."

sentences.zh: 儻旬浹之間，大軍東至，即賊必退。

translations.literal: Perhaps within ten days the great army will arrive from the east—then the bandits are certain to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days the main army should arrive from the east, and the rebels will retreat."

sentences.zh: 」仁矩曰：「蜀兵懦，安能當我精甲！

translations.literal: " Renju said: "Shu troops are cowardly—how can they withstand my fine armor!
translations.idiomatic: " Renju said, "Shu soldiers are soft. How can they stand against our elite armor!

sentences.zh: 」即驅之出戰，兵未交，為賊所敗。

translations.literal: " He immediately drove them out to battle; the troops had not yet engaged when they were defeated by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: " He forced them out to fight at once. Before the lines met, the enemy routed them.

sentences.zh: 既而城陷，仁矩被擒，舉族為璋所害。

translations.literal: Soon after the city fell, Renju was captured, and his whole clan was harmed by Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: The city soon fell. Renju was taken, and Zhang slaughtered his entire family.

sentences.zh: 康思立，晉陽人也。

translations.literal: Kang Sili was a man of Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Sili was a native of Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 少善騎射，事武皇為爪牙，署河東親騎軍使。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled at mounted archery, served Emperor Wu as a claw-and-fang man, and was appointed commander of the Hedong personal mounted guard.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he excelled at mounted archery, served Emperor Wu as a personal guard, and was made commander of the Hedong personal cavalry.

sentences.zh: 莊宗嗣位，從解圍於上黨，敗梁人於柏鄉，及平薊兵，後戰於河上，皆有功，累承製加檢校戶部尚書，右突騎指揮使。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong succeeded, he followed in raising the siege at Shangdang, defeated Liang men at Baixiang, and in pacifying Ji troops and later fighting on the Yellow River—all had merit; repeatedly received edicts adding Acting Household Minister, Right Vanguard Cavalry Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhuangzong he helped lift the siege at Shangdang, defeated Liang forces at Baixiang, helped pacify the Ji campaign, and later fought on the Yellow River, earning repeated honors. He rose to acting household minister and commander of the right vanguard cavalry.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位，繼改軍帥，賜忠勇拱衛功臣，加檢校尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he was again changed to army commander, granted the merit title Loyal and Brave Arch Guardian, and added Acting Censor-in-Chief, Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhuangzong's accession he was made an army commander, granted the merit title Loyal and Brave Arch Guardian, and promoted to acting censor-in-chief and right vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天成元年，授應州刺史，尋移嵐州，充北面諸蕃部族都監。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng he was appointed Yingzhou prefect, soon moved to Lanzhou, and filled the post of superintendent of all northern frontier tribal groups.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng 1 he became prefect of Yingzhou, soon transferred to Lanzhou as superintendent of the northern frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷宿州團練使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was moved to Suzhou regimental trainer.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made regimental trainer of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，領昭武軍節度、利巴集等州觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he led Zhaowu Army command and the observation and disposition commissioner of Li, Ba, Ji, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he took command of the Zhaowu army and became observation commissioner over Li, Ba, Ji, and related prefectures.

sentences.zh: 改賜耀忠保節功臣。

translations.literal: His granted merit title was changed to Glorious Loyalty, Protecting the Realm.
translations.idiomatic: He was re-granted the merit title Glorious Loyalty, Protecting the Realm.

sentences.zh: 長興初，朝廷舉兵討東川董璋，詔監西面行營軍馬都指揮使。

translations.literal: Early in Changxing the court raised troops to punish Eastern Rivers Dong Zhang, and edicted him to supervise the western campaign army horse commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Changxing, when the court marched against Dong Zhang of Eastern Shu, Sili was ordered to supervise the western campaign's cavalry command.

sentences.zh: 二年，移鎮陝州。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to command Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was transferred to Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：潞王至靈寶，思立謀固守陝城以俟康義誠。

translations.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror: When the Prince of Lu reached Lingbao, Sili planned to hold fast to Shaan city and await Kang Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: (Comprehensive Mirror: When the Prince of Lu reached Lingbao, Sili planned to hold Shaanzhou and wait for Kang Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 先是，捧聖五百騎戍陝，為潞王前鋒，至城下，呼城上人曰：「禁軍十萬已奉新帝，爾輩數人奚為！

translations.literal: Earlier, five hundred Pingsheng cavalry garrisoned Shaan as the Prince of Lu's vanguard; reaching below the walls, they called to those atop the wall: "The forbidden army of one hundred thousand has already received the new emperor—what are you few doing!
translations.idiomatic: Earlier five hundred Pingsheng horsemen had garrisoned Shaan as the prince's vanguard. At the walls they shouted: "A hundred thousand imperial guards have already acclaimed the new emperor—what are you few still doing!

sentences.zh: 徒累一城人塗地耳！

translations.literal: You will only involve the people of one city in bloodshed on the ground!
translations.idiomatic: You will only drown this whole city in blood!"

sentences.zh: 」於是捧聖卒爭出迎，思立不能禁，不得已，亦出迎。）〉

translations.literal: Thereupon the Pingsheng soldiers vied to go out and welcome them; Sili could not forbid it, had no choice, and also went out to welcome them.)〉
translations.idiomatic: At that the Pingsheng troops rushed out to welcome them. Sili could not stop them and had no choice but to go out and submit as well.)〉

sentences.zh: 清泰初，改授邢台，累官至檢校太傅，封會稽郡開國侯。

translations.literal: Early in Qingtai he was reassigned to Xingtai, rising through offices to Acting Grand Tutor, enfeoffed as Marquis who Opens the State of Kuaiji Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qingtai he was reassigned to Xingtai, rose to acting grand tutor, and was enfeoffed as Marquis who Opens Kuaiji Commandery.

sentences.zh: 二年，入為右神武統軍。

translations.literal: In the second year he entered the capital as Right Divine Martial Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he entered court as commander of the Right Divine Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 三年，充北面行營馬軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the third year he filled the post of northern campaign army cavalry commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became commander of the northern campaign's cavalry.

sentences.zh: 是歲閏十一月，卒於軍，年六十三。

translations.literal: That year, in the intercalary eleventh month, he died in the army at age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: That year, in the intercalary eleventh month, he died on campaign at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 張敬達，字志通，代州人，小字生鐵。

translations.literal: Zhang Jingda, style Zhizong, a man of Dai Prefecture, childhood name Raw Iron.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingda, courtesy name Zhizong, was a native of Dai Prefecture; his childhood name was Raw Iron.

sentences.zh: 父審，素有勇，事武皇為列校，曆廳直軍使，同光初，卒於軍。

translations.literal: His father Shen had always had courage, served Emperor Wu as a company commander, passed through Hall Direct Army Commander; in early Tongguang he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shen was a man of courage who served Emperor Wu as a company commander and rose to hall direct army commander; he died on campaign in early Tongguang.

sentences.zh: 敬達少以騎射著名，莊宗知之，召令繼父職；

translations.literal: Jingda in youth was famous for mounted archery; Zhuangzong knew it and summoned him to succeed his father's post;
translations.idiomatic: Jingda won fame in youth for mounted archery. Zhuangzong noticed him and summoned him to succeed his father's post;

sentences.zh: 平河南有功，繼加檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: In pacifying Henan he had merit, and was further added Acting Works Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in the pacification of Henan and was further made acting minister of works.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，曆捧聖指揮使、檢校尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, he passed through Pingsheng Commander and Acting Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong came to the throne he served as commander of the Pingsheng guard and acting left vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 長興中，改河東馬步軍都指揮使，超授檢校司徒，領欽州刺史。

translations.literal: In Changxing he was changed to Hedong horse-and-foot army commander-in-chief, leap-promoted Acting Minister of Works, and led Qinzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: During Changxing he became commander of the Hedong horse-and-foot forces, was abruptly promoted to acting minister of works, and made prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，加檢校太保、應州節度使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was added Acting Grand Mentor and Yingzhou military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made acting grand mentor and military governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷雲州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was moved to Yun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 時以契丹率族帳自黑榆林挎剌泊至沒越泊，雲借漢界水草，敬達每聚兵塞下，以遏其衝。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan led their tribal tents from Black Willow Forest Kualapo to Meiyuepo; Yun borrowed Han frontier grass and water—Jingda every time gathered troops below the passes to block their rush.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Khitan drove their tribal camps from Black Willow Forest and Kualapo to Meiyuepo to graze on Han frontier pasture. Jingda repeatedly massed troops along the border passes to block their advance.

sentences.zh: 契丹竟不敢南牧，邊人賴之。

translations.literal: The Khitan in the end did not dare pasture south; the frontier people relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan never dared drive their herds south, and the frontier people owed their security to him.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，自彭門移鎮平陽，加檢校太傅，從石敬瑭為北面兵馬副總管，仍屯兵雁門。

translations.literal: In Qingtai he moved from Peng Gate to command Pingyang, was added Acting Grand Tutor, followed Shi Jingtang as northern army horse-and-foot deputy commander-in-chief, and still garrisoned troops at Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingtai he was transferred from Pengmen to Pingyang, made acting grand tutor, and served under Shi Jingtang as deputy commander of the northern forces while keeping his troops at Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 未幾，晉高祖建義，末帝詔以敬達為北面行營都招討使，仍使悉引部下兵圍太原，以定州節度使楊光遠副焉。

translations.literal: Before long, the Jin High Ancestor raised his righteous cause; the Last Emperor edicted Jingda as northern campaign commander-in-chief for recruitment and punishment, still ordering him to lead all subordinate troops to besiege Taiyuan, with Dingzhou military governor Yang Guangyuan as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Jin High Ancestor rose in revolt. The Last Emperor appointed Jingda commander of the northern campaign to recruit and punish the rebels and ordered him to bring all his troops to besiege Taiyuan, with Yang Guangyuan, military governor of Dingzhou, as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 尋統兵三萬，營於晉安鄉。

translations.literal: Soon he commanded thirty thousand troops and encamped at Jin'an township.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took command of thirty thousand men and encamped at Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 末帝自六月繼有詔促令攻取，敬達設長城連柵、雲梯飛炮，使工者運其巧思，窮土木之力。

translations.literal: From the sixth month the Last Emperor repeatedly had edicts urging attack; Jingda set long walls, linked palisades, cloud ladders, and flying catapults, making craftsmen deploy their clever designs and exhausting the strength of earth and wood.
translations.idiomatic: From the sixth month the Last Emperor kept issuing orders to attack. Jingda built long walls, linked palisades, siege towers, and trebuchets, pressing craftsmen to exhaust every device of wood and earth.

sentences.zh: 時督事者每有所構，則暴風大雨，平地水深數尺，而城柵崩墮，竟不能合其圍。

translations.literal: Whenever those supervising the works had something constructed, then violent wind and great rain came; level ground water several feet deep, and walls and palisades collapsed and fell—ultimately they could not close the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the engineers built some new work, violent storms would flood the plain several feet deep and collapse the walls and palisades, so the siege could never be closed.

sentences.zh: 九月，契丹至，敬達大敗，尋為所圍。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Khitan arrived; Jingda was greatly defeated and soon was surrounded.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Khitan arrived. Jingda suffered a crushing defeat and was soon surrounded.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖及蕃眾自晉安寨南門外，長百餘里，闊五十里，布以氈帳，用毛索掛鈴，而部伍多犬，以備警急。

translations.literal: The Jin High Ancestor and the barbarian masses from outside the Jin'an stockade south gate stretched more than a hundred li, fifty li wide, spread with felt tents, using wool ropes hung with bells, and the ranks had many dogs to guard against sudden alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin High Ancestor and the barbarian hosts stretched more than a hundred li south of the Jin'an stockade gate, fifty li across, pitched in felt tents with wool ropes hung with bells, and their ranks kept many dogs to sound the alarm.

sentences.zh: 營中嘗有夜遁者，出則犬吠鈴動，跬步不能行焉。

translations.literal: In the camp if there was one who fled by night, going out then dogs barked and bells moved—a half-step could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who tried to flee at night set the dogs barking and the bells ringing, so that not a half-step could be taken.

sentences.zh: 自是敬達與麾下部曲五萬人，馬萬匹，無由四奔，但見穹廬如崗阜相屬，諸軍相顧失色。

translations.literal: From this Jingda with his command banners and subordinate ranks of fifty thousand men, ten thousand horses, had no way to flee in the four directions, but saw only domed tents like hillocks linked in succession—the armies looked at one another and lost color.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Jingda and his fifty thousand men and ten thousand horses had no path of escape in any direction. They saw only dome tents piled like hills, and the army turned pale.

sentences.zh: 始則削木篩糞，以飼其馬，日望朝廷救軍，及漸羸死，則與將士分食之，馬盡食殫。

translations.literal: At first they shaved wood and sifted dung to feed their horses, daily looking to the court's rescue army; as they gradually grew lean and died, then they divided and ate them with officers and soldiers—the horses all eaten up.
translations.idiomatic: At first they fed the horses on shaved wood and sifted dung while waiting for imperial relief. As the horses weakened and died, officers and soldiers ate them until none remained.

sentences.zh: 副將楊光遠、次將安審琦知不濟，勸敬達宜早降以求自安。

translations.literal: Deputy commander Yang Guangyuan and second commander An Shenqi knew it would not succeed, and urged Jingda that he ought early to surrender to seek his own safety.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Yang Guangyuan and second-in-command An Shenqi saw defeat was certain and urged Jingda to surrender early for his own safety.

sentences.zh: 敬達曰：「吾受恩於明宗，位曆方鎮，主上授我大柄，而失律如此，已有愧於心也。

translations.literal: Jingda said: "I received favor from Mingzong, my posts passing through frontier commands; the sovereign entrusted me with great authority, yet I lost discipline like this—I already have shame in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Jingda said: "Mingzong favored me and set me over the frontier commands. The sovereign gave me supreme authority, and I have failed so badly that I am already ashamed in my own heart.

sentences.zh: 今救軍在近，旦暮雪恥有期，諸公何相迫耶！

translations.literal: Now the rescue army is near; morning and evening the snow of shame has its term—why do you gentlemen press me!
translations.idiomatic: Relief is close at hand, and we may yet wipe away this disgrace before long. Why do you press me so!"

sentences.zh: 待勢窮，則請殺吾，攜首以降，亦未為晚。

translations.literal: Wait until our strength is exhausted, then please kill me and carry my head to surrender—it is still not late.
translations.idiomatic: When we are truly spent, you may kill me and offer my head in surrender—that will still be in time."

sentences.zh: 」光遠、審琦知敬達意未決，恐坐成魚肉，遂斬敬達以降。

translations.literal: " Guangyuan and Shenqi knew Jingda's intent was not yet decided, feared sitting to become fish flesh, and thereupon beheaded Jingda to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " Guangyuan and Shenqi saw that Jingda would not decide and feared becoming helpless prey, so they cut off Jingda's head and surrendered.

sentences.zh: （《契丹國志》：楊光遠謀害張敬達，諸將高行周陰為之備，敬達疏於防禦，推遠行周等。

translations.literal: (History of the Khitan State: Yang Guangyuan plotted to harm Zhang Jingda; the generals Gao Xingzhou secretly made preparations for him; Jingda was lax in defense and pushed authority onto Guangyuan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: (History of the Khitan State: Yang Guangyuan plotted to kill Zhang Jingda. The general Gao Xingzhou secretly prepared against it, but Jingda was careless in defense and delegated authority to Guangyuan and others.

sentences.zh: 清晨，光遠上謁，見敬達左右無人，遂殺之。）〉

translations.literal: At dawn Guangyuan went up to pay respects; seeing no one at Jingda's side, he thereupon killed him.)〉
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Guangyuan came to pay his respects, found no one beside Jingda, and killed him.)〉
